text:
Boosting a post is not the same as running ads.

A cafe in Anna Nagar boosts a nice reel. It gets likes, a few new followers, and zero table bookings.

Because the boost was set up for reach, not enquiries.

So before you spend more, ask one thing: what should someone do right after seeing this ad? Call? Message? Book?

If you can't answer that, your ad can't either.

text:
Your website gets visitors. So why is nobody enquiring?

Most of the time it's not the design. It's the first screen.

A clinic in Velachery doesn't need a fancy slider. It needs:
→ what you do, in one line
→ where you are
→ one clear button: Book an appointment

If a visitor has to scroll just to figure out what to do next, they leave.

Want a website that actually brings enquiries? Book a free consultation (link in the reply).
headline: Visitors but no enquiries? Fix the first screen.
linkedin_hook: One shoot day can give you a month of reels. But only if you plan it before the camera comes out.

text:
Your reels get views. So why are the DMs empty?

Usually it's not the content. It's the profile people land on after the reel.

→ The bio doesn't say what you sell or where you are
→ There's no clear way to book or order
→ The last post is three weeks old
→ The reel ends without telling people what to do next

A boutique in T. Nagar can fix all four this week.

text:
Your ads are reaching people who will never visit you.

A salon in Anna Nagar doesn't need clicks from Tambaram.
Those people won't travel 20 km for a haircut.

But if your ad is set to all of Chennai, that's where your budget goes.

So pick the area your customers actually come from.
Show them one clear offer.
Make it easy to send a message.

text:
Myth: you need to post every day to get enquiries.

Fact: posting daily with no plan just tires you out.

A cafe in Anna Nagar that posts 3 planned reels a week, each one showing the menu, the price and how to reach them, gives people a reason to message.

Random daily posts just give them something to scroll past.

So plan the month first. Then post.
